source_text: Sed nimis sum ipsa rerum reverentia eius qua de agitur contentionis oblitus. Miror enim ambigi de Dei aequitate potuisse, cum constet in Traducianorum synagogis nihil de eius iniquitate dubitari.
pass_a_gloss: But by the very reverence of the matters I have too much forgotten the contention that is being treated. For I marvel that it could have been doubted about God's fairness, when it stands that in the synagogues of the advocates of inherited sin nothing is doubted about his injustice.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent

pass_b_english: But my very reverence for these matters has made me forget too completely the dispute at hand. I marvel that God’s fairness could have been questioned, although it is well established that in the assemblies of the advocates of inherited sin there is no doubt at all about his unfairness.

choices.why: Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.
Scripture's destruction of iniquitas is the Law's purpose; keep moral injustice.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
